title: सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीको प्रभावकारिता: एक अध्ययन { A Study: Effectiveness of Continuing Student Assessment System in Community Schools
nepali: यो अध्ययन‘ सामुदायिक विद्यालयमा निरन्तर विद्याथी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीको प्रभावकारिता ःएक अध्ययन’ शीर्षकमा गरिएको हो । अवस्था अध्ययन ९ऋबकभ क्तगमथ०को रूपमा याअध्ययन पत्र तयार पारिएको हो । यसअन्तर्गत नेपालको शैक्षिक पृष्ठभूमि, विद्यालयीय विद्याथीमूल्याङ्कन परिपाटी र निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कनको छोटो ऐतिहासिक झलक प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ ।यसमा समस्याको परिचय, औचित्य र उद्दश्य प्रस्तुत गरिएका छन । ती उद्देश्यहरू यस पकारछन ः नेपालमा सामुदायिक विद्यालय अन्तर्गतका प्राथमिक तहका विद्यार्थीहरूको मूल्याङ्कनकाप्रचलित विधिहरूको जानकारी दिन, निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीमा देखिएका समस्याहरूपत्ता लगाउनु, निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीलाई अझ बढी उपलब्धिमूलक बनाउनका लागिदेखिएका समस्या समाधानका उपायहरु पत्ता लगाउनु रहेको छ । यस अध्ययनको सीमा अन्तर्गत निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणाली लागू भएका नेपालकापाँच जिल्लामध्ये चितवन जिल्लाको भरतपुर नगरपालिका भित्रका चार सामुदायिक विद्यालय(नारायणी उच्च मा.वि., शरदपुर मा.वि., रत्ननगर मा.वि. र नयाँ किरण मा.विद्यालय) लाइसमेटिएको छ । यस अध्ययनका लागि तयार पारिएका प्रश्न र अध्ययन पत्र अन्तर्गत उल्लेखगरिएका पारिभाषिक शब्दको परिभाषा दिने काम गरिएको छ । सम्बन्धित साहित्यको सिंहावलोकन अन्तर्गत निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कनको सद्धान्तिकअवधारणा प्रस्तुत गरिएका छ । यो प्रणाली नेपालमा विशेष गरी प्राथमिक तहमा हुने गरेकाशैक्षिक क्षति कम गर्ने उद्दश्यले तत्कालीन सरकार शिक्षा मन्त्रालयले शैक्षिक सत्र २०५७÷०५८बाट निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणाली लागू गर्ने नीतिअनुरूप विभिन्न विद्यार्थीको मूल्याङ्कनकासूचक(अनसूचीमा उल्लेख) बाट अभिलेख राखी श्रेणी छुटयाई कक्षोन्नति गन परिपाटीअनुरूपचितवनमा पनि परीक्षणका रूपमा लागू गरिएको हा । यस अध्ययनसंग सम्बन्धित साहित्यकासिंहावलोकन गर्दा यस प्रणालीको सैद्धान्तिक र व्यवहारिक पक्षको वारेमा केही व्यक्ति वासंस्थाहरुद्वारा उल्लेख गरिएको पाइन्छ । अध्ययन विधिका रुपमा यस अध्ययन क्षेत्रकाविद्यालयहरूको विभिन्न पक्षको तथ्याङ्कलाई स्रोतका रूपमा लिइएको छ । यसअन्तर्गत चारविद्यालयका ८० जना विद्यार्थी, चारजना प्रधानाध्यापक, १२ जना कक्षा शिक्षक, १२ जनाअभिभावक र एकजना स्रोतव्यक्ति गरी जम्मा १०९ जनालाई अध्ययनको जनसंख्या मानिएकाछ । सकसम्म फरक फरक अवस्थामा रहेका विद्यालयलाई आधार लिइएको छ । अध्ययनलाइवस्तुगत र प्रामाणिक बनाउनका लागि विद्यालय भ्रमण, पश्नावली परीक्षण, अभिलेख, निरीक्षण, प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाट, अन्तरवार्ता, अवलोकन आदि पद्वतिलाई आधार मानिएको छ । यस अध्ययनकाक्रममा प्राप्त सूचना तथा तथ्याङ्कलाई तालिकीकरण गरी विवेचना, व्याख्या, विश्लेषण, तुलना रमूल्याङ्कन पद्धतिलाई विश्लषणको आधार वनाइएको छ । निरन्तर विद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणालीको प्रभावकारितामा देखिएका समस्या केलाएरसमाधानका उपायहरू सुझाइएको छ । यस प्रणालीको प्रभावकारितामा विद्यार्थी, शिक्षक,अभिभावक, प्रधानाध्यापक, स्रोतव्यक्ति साथै जि.शि.का.संग समयको अभाव, हेलचेक्रयाइँ,उदासीनताजस्ता समस्याका साथै उक्त समस्या समाधानार्थ उपायहरू उल्लेख गरिएका छन ।यसमा कार्यक्रम पूर्वतयारीका साथ ल्याउनुपर्ने, दण्ड सजायको व्यवस्था क्रियान्वयन हुनुपन,अनुगमन मूल्याङ्कन पद्धतिलाई प्रभावकारी वनाउनु पर्ने, विद्यालयको भौतिक पूर्वाधार व्यवस्थितहुनुपर्ने आदि उपायहरू उल्लेख गरिएका छन । अन्त्यमा यस शोधको सारांश, निष्कर्ष र सुझावलाइ प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । या निरन्तरविद्यार्थी मूल्याङ्कन प्रणाली जुन उद्देश्यका साथ तत्कालीन सरकारले शैक्षिक सत्र ०५७÷०५८बाट लागु गरेको थियो । त्यसको कार्यान्वयनको छोटो समयमा नै प्रभावकारिता शून्य रहेको यसअध्ययनमा पाइएको छ । यस क्षेत्रका विभिन्न सरोकारवालाहरु बेजिम्मेवार रहेको उल्लेख गनकासाथै यो कार्यक्रम पूणतया असफल भएको उल्लेख गरिएको छ । यस प्रणालीलाई असफल हुननदिनका लागि शिक्षा मन्त्रालयदेखि अभिभावकसम्मका विभिन्न सरोकारवालाहरुको पक्षबाटगरिनुपर्ने सुधारका कुरालाई ठोस रूपमा उल्लेख समेत गरिएको छ । यसमा कार्यक्रम पूर्वतयारीका साथ ल्याउनु पर्ने, माथिल्लो निकायबाट सुपरिवेक्षण हुनु पन, सबै सरोकारवालाहरुजवाफदेही हुनु पर्ने, कर्तव्यहीन व्यक्ति वा संस्थालाई आवश्यक कारवाही गरिनु पर्ने जस्ताःसुझावहरु प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । अन्त्यमा थप अध्ययनका लागि केही शीर्षकहरु प्रस्तुत गरिएका छन ।
american_english:
This study was carried out under the title "Effectiveness of the Continuous Student Assessment System in Community Schools: A Study."
The study paper was prepared in the form of a case study.
Under it, Nepal's educational background, school-level student assessment practice, and a brief historical glimpse of continuous student assessment are presented.
In it, the introduction of the problem, its rationale and objectives are presented.
Those objectives are as follows: to provide information about the methods prevalent in assessing primary-level students under community schools in Nepal, to find out the problems seen in the continuous student assessment system, and to find out ways to solve the problems seen in order to make the continuous student assessment system more achievement-oriented.
Under the scope of this study, four community schools within Bharatpur Municipality of Chitwan district — Narayani Higher Secondary School, Sharadpur Secondary School, Ratnanagar Secondary School and Naya Kiran Secondary School — among the five districts of Nepal where the continuous student assessment system has been implemented, are included.
The questions prepared for this study and the definitions of the technical terms mentioned under the study paper have been given.
Under the review of related literature, the theoretical concept of continuous student assessment is presented.
This system was implemented by the then government, the Ministry of Education, from the academic session 2057/58 with the objective of reducing educational loss especially at the primary level in Nepal; in line with the policy of implementing the continuous student assessment system, records were kept on the basis of various student assessment indicators (mentioned in the list), grades were assigned and classes were promoted; in Chitwan too it was implemented on a trial basis.
In reviewing the literature related to this study, it is found that some individuals and organizations have mentioned the theoretical and practical sides of this system.
As the study method, data on various aspects of the schools in this study area were taken as the source.
Under this, a total of 109 people — 80 students, four head teachers, 12 class teachers, 12 parents and one resource person from four schools — were taken as the population of the study.
Schools in as different situations as possible were taken as the basis.
To make the study objective and authentic, methods such as school visits, questionnaire testing, records, inspection, direct meetings, interviews and observation were taken as the basis.
The information and data obtained in the course of this study were tabulated, and the methods of discussion, explanation, analysis, comparison and evaluation were made the basis of analysis.
The problems seen in the effectiveness of the continuous student assessment system have been examined and solutions suggested.
In the effectiveness of this system, problems such as lack of time among students, teachers, parents, head teachers, resource persons and the District Education Office, negligence and indifference have been mentioned, along with measures to solve those problems.
In it, measures such as bringing the program with prior preparation, implementing a system of punishment, making the monitoring and evaluation method effective, and keeping the school's physical infrastructure in order have been mentioned.
At the end, the summary, conclusions and suggestions of this research have been presented.
This study has found that the effectiveness of the continuous student assessment system, which the then government implemented from the academic session 057/58 with a certain objective, was zero within a short time of its implementation.
Along with stating that the various stakeholders in this area were irresponsible, it has been mentioned that this program failed completely.
In order to keep this system from failing, the reforms that various stakeholders, from the Ministry of Education down to parents, need to make have also been mentioned concretely.
In it, suggestions such as bringing the program with prior preparation, supervision from the higher body, all stakeholders being accountable, and taking necessary action against irresponsible persons or institutions have been presented.
At the end, some titles for further study have been presented.

The problems that have arisen in the effectiveness of the continuous student assessment system have been sifted, and remedies have been suggested.
In the effectiveness of this system, problems such as want of time on the part of pupils, teachers, parents, head teachers, resource persons and the District Education Office, negligence and indifference have been mentioned, together with measures for their solution.
In it, measures such as introducing the programme with prior preparation, putting a system of penalty into effect, rendering the method of monitoring and evaluation effective, and keeping the school's physical infrastructure in order have been mentioned.

Besides stating that the various stakeholders in this field were irresponsible, it is mentioned that this programme failed utterly.

australian_english:
This study was done under the title "Effectiveness of the Continuous Student Assessment System in Community Schools: A Study."
The study paper was put together as a case study.
It sets out Nepal's education background, the way schools assess students, and a short look back at the history of continuous student assessment.
It presents the problem, why it matters, and the objectives.
The objectives are: to give information about the methods used to assess primary-level students in community schools in Nepal, to find the problems that have turned up in the continuous student assessment system, and to find ways to fix those problems so the system does more to lift achievement.
The study covers four community schools in Bharatpur Municipality, Chitwan district — Narayani Higher Secondary School, Sharadpur Secondary School, Ratnanagar Secondary School and Naya Kiran Secondary School — out of the five districts in Nepal where the continuous student assessment system has been rolled out.
The questions prepared for the study and the definitions of the technical terms used in the study paper are given.
Under the review of related literature, the theoretical idea behind continuous student assessment is laid out.
The system was brought in by the then government, the Ministry of Education, from the 2057/58 academic session to cut educational loss, especially at primary level in Nepal; under the policy of rolling out continuous student assessment, records were kept using different student assessment indicators (listed), grades were given and students were promoted; in Chitwan it was trialled too.
In the literature review for this study, it turns out some individuals and organisations have written about the theory and practice of this system.
For method, data on different aspects of the schools in the study area were used as the source.
Under this, 109 people in total — 80 students, four head teachers, 12 class teachers, 12 parents and one resource person across four schools — were taken as the study population.
Schools in as many different situations as possible were used as the basis.
To keep the study objective and trustworthy, school visits, questionnaire trials, records, inspection, face-to-face meetings, interviews and observation were used as the basis.
The information and data gathered during the study were put into tables, and discussion, explanation, analysis, comparison and evaluation were used as the basis for analysis.
The problems showing up in the effectiveness of the continuous student assessment system have been picked apart, and fixes suggested.
For the system's effectiveness, problems like everyone — students, teachers, parents, head teachers, resource persons and the District Education Office — being short of time, plus negligence and indifference, are mentioned, along with ways to fix them.
It mentions measures like bringing the program in with proper preparation, putting a penalty system in place, making monitoring and evaluation work properly, and getting the school's physical infrastructure sorted.
At the end, the summary, conclusions and suggestions of the research are presented.
The study found that the continuous student assessment system, brought in by the then government from the 057/58 academic session for a particular purpose, had zero effectiveness within a short time of being implemented.
As well as saying the various stakeholders in the area were irresponsible, it says the program failed completely.
To stop the system failing, the study also spells out concretely what reforms different stakeholders, from the Ministry of Education right down to parents, need to make.
It puts forward suggestions like bringing the program in with proper preparation, supervision from the higher body, all stakeholders being accountable, and necessary action against irresponsible people or institutions.
At the end, some titles for further study are presented.
